title: תהילים פרק 18
english_audio_source: YouVersion — The Listener’s Bible®: KJV Edition
verses: לַמְנַצֵּחַ, לְעֶבֶד יְהוָה--לְדָוִד: אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר, לַיהוָה, אֶת-דִּבְרֵי, הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת-- בְּיוֹם הִצִּיל-יְהוָה אוֹתוֹ מִכַּף כָּל-אֹיְבָיו, וּמִיַּד שָׁאוּל.
וַיֹּאמַר-- אֶרְחָמְךָ יְהוָה חִזְקִי.
יְהוָה, סַלְעִי וּמְצוּדָתִי-- וּמְפַלְטִי: אֵלִי צוּרִי, אֶחֱסֶה-בּוֹ; מָגִנִּי וְקֶרֶן-יִשְׁעִי, מִשְׂגַּבִּי.
מְהֻלָּל, אֶקְרָא יְהוָה; וּמִן-אֹיְבַי, אִוָּשֵׁעַ.
אֲפָפוּנִי חֶבְלֵי-מָוֶת; וְנַחֲלֵי בְלִיַּעַל יְבַעֲתוּנִי.
חֶבְלֵי שְׁאוֹל סְבָבוּנִי; קִדְּמוּנִי, מוֹקְשֵׁי מָוֶת.
בַּצַּר-לִי, אֶקְרָא יְהוָה-- וְאֶל-אֱלֹהַי אֲשַׁוֵּעַ: יִשְׁמַע מֵהֵיכָלוֹ קוֹלִי; וְשַׁוְעָתִי, לְפָנָיו תָּבוֹא בְאָזְנָיו.
וַתִּגְעַשׁ וַתִּרְעַשׁ, הָאָרֶץ-- וּמוֹסְדֵי הָרִים יִרְגָּזוּ; וַיִּתְגָּעֲשׁוּ, כִּי-חָרָה לוֹ.
עָלָה עָשָׁן, בְּאַפּוֹ-- וְאֵשׁ-מִפִּיו תֹּאכֵל; גֶּחָלִים, בָּעֲרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ.
וַיֵּט שָׁמַיִם, וַיֵּרַד; וַעֲרָפֶל, תַּחַת רַגְלָיו.
וַיִּרְכַּב עַל-כְּרוּב, וַיָּעֹף; וַיֵּדֶא, עַל-כַּנְפֵי-רוּחַ.
יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ, סִתְרוֹ-- סְבִיבוֹתָיו סֻכָּתוֹ; חֶשְׁכַת-מַיִם, עָבֵי שְׁחָקִים.
מִנֹּגַהּ, נֶגְדּוֹ: עָבָיו עָבְרוּ--בָּרָד, וְגַחֲלֵי-אֵשׁ.
וַיַּרְעֵם בַּשָּׁמַיִם, יְהוָה--וְעֶלְיוֹן, יִתֵּן קֹלוֹ; בָּרָד, וְגַחֲלֵי-אֵשׁ.
וַיִּשְׁלַח חִצָּיו, וַיְפִיצֵם; וּבְרָקִים רָב, וַיְהֻמֵּם.
וַיֵּרָאוּ, אֲפִיקֵי מַיִם, וַיִּגָּלוּ, מוֹסְדוֹת תֵּבֵל: מִגַּעֲרָתְךָ יְהוָה-- מִנִּשְׁמַת, רוּחַ אַפֶּךָ.
יִשְׁלַח מִמָּרוֹם, יִקָּחֵנִי; יַמְשֵׁנִי, מִמַּיִם רַבִּים.
יַצִּילֵנִי, מֵאֹיְבִי עָז; וּמִשֹּׂנְאַי, כִּי-אָמְצוּ מִמֶּנִּי.
יְקַדְּמוּנִי בְיוֹם-אֵידִי; וַיְהִי-יְהוָה לְמִשְׁעָן לִי.
וַיּוֹצִיאֵנִי לַמֶּרְחָב; יְחַלְּצֵנִי, כִּי חָפֵץ בִּי.
יִגְמְלֵנִי יְהוָה כְּצִדְקִי; כְּבֹר יָדַי, יָשִׁיב לִי.
כִּי-שָׁמַרְתִּי, דַּרְכֵי יְהוָה; וְלֹא-רָשַׁעְתִּי, מֵאֱלֹהָי.
כִּי כָל-מִשְׁפָּטָיו לְנֶגְדִּי; וְחֻקֹּתָיו, לֹא-אָסִיר מֶנִּי.
וָאֱהִי תָמִים עִמּוֹ; וָאֶשְׁתַּמֵּר, מֵעֲוֺנִי.
וַיָּשֶׁב-יְהוָה לִי כְצִדְקִי; כְּבֹר יָדַי, לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו.
עִם-חָסִיד תִּתְחַסָּד; עִם-גְּבַר תָּמִים, תִּתַּמָּם.
עִם-נָבָר תִּתְבָּרָר; וְעִם-עִקֵּשׁ, תִּתְפַּתָּל.
כִּי-אַתָּה, עַם-עָנִי תוֹשִׁיעַ; וְעֵינַיִם רָמוֹת תַּשְׁפִּיל.
כִּי-אַתָּה, תָּאִיר נֵרִי; יְהוָה אֱלֹהַי, יַגִּיהַּ חָשְׁכִּי.
כִּי-בְךָ, אָרֻץ גְּדוּד; וּבֵאלֹהַי, אֲדַלֶּג-שׁוּר.
הָאֵל, תָּמִים דַּרְכּוֹ: אִמְרַת-יְהוָה צְרוּפָה; מָגֵן הוּא, לְכֹל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ.
כִּי מִי אֱלוֹהַּ, מִבַּלְעֲדֵי יְהוָה; וּמִי צוּר, זוּלָתִי אֱלֹהֵינוּ.
הָאֵל, הַמְאַזְּרֵנִי חָיִל; וַיִּתֵּן תָּמִים דַּרְכִּי.
מְשַׁוֶּה רַגְלַי, כָּאַיָּלוֹת; וְעַל בָּמֹתַי, יַעֲמִידֵנִי.
מְלַמֵּד יָדַי, לַמִּלְחָמָה; וְנִחֲתָה קֶשֶׁת-נְחוּשָׁה, זְרוֹעֹתָי.
וַתִּתֶּן-לִי, מָגֵן יִשְׁעֶךָ: וִימִינְךָ תִסְעָדֵנִי; וְעַנְוַתְךָ תַרְבֵּנִי.
תַּרְחִיב צַעֲדִי תַחְתָּי; וְלֹא מָעֲדוּ, קַרְסֻלָּי.
אֶרְדּוֹף אוֹיְבַי, וְאַשִּׂיגֵם; וְלֹא-אָשׁוּב, עַד-כַּלּוֹתָם.
אֶמְחָצֵם, וְלֹא-יֻכְלוּ קוּם; יִפְּלוּ, תַּחַת רַגְלָי.
וַתְּאַזְּרֵנִי חַיִל, לַמִּלְחָמָה; תַּכְרִיעַ קָמַי תַּחְתָּי.
וְאֹיְבַי, נָתַתָּה לִּי עֹרֶף; וּמְשַׂנְאַי, אַצְמִיתֵם.
יְשַׁוְּעוּ וְאֵין-מוֹשִׁיעַ; עַל-יְהוָה, וְלֹא עָנָם.
וְאֶשְׁחָקֵם, כְּעָפָר עַל-פְּנֵי-רוּחַ; כְּטִיט חוּצוֹת אֲרִיקֵם.
תְּפַלְּטֵנִי, מֵרִיבֵי-עָם: תְּשִׂימֵנִי, לְרֹאשׁ גּוֹיִם; עַם לֹא-יָדַעְתִּי יַעַבְדוּנִי.
לְשֵׁמַע אֹזֶן, יִשָּׁמְעוּ לִי; בְּנֵי-נֵכָר, יְכַחֲשׁוּ-לִי.
בְּנֵי-נֵכָר יִבֹּלוּ; וְיַחְרְגוּ, מִמִּסְגְּרוֹתֵיהֶם.
חַי-יְהוָה, וּבָרוּךְ צוּרִי; וְיָרוּם, אֱלוֹהֵי יִשְׁעִי.
הָאֵל--הַנּוֹתֵן נְקָמוֹת לִי; וַיַּדְבֵּר עַמִּים תַּחְתָּי.
מְפַלְּטִי, מֵאֹיְבָי: אַף מִן-קָמַי, תְּרוֹמְמֵנִי; מֵאִישׁ חָמָס, תַּצִּילֵנִי.
עַל-כֵּן, אוֹדְךָ בַגּוֹיִם יְהוָה; וּלְשִׁמְךָ אֲזַמֵּרָה.
מַגְדִּל, יְשׁוּעוֹת מַלְכּוֹ: וְעֹשֶׂה חֶסֶד, לִמְשִׁיחוֹ--לְדָוִד וּלְזַרְעוֹ; עַד-עוֹלָם.
english: I will love thee, O LORD, my strength.

The LORD
is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation,
and my high tower.

I will call upon the LORD,
who is worthy to be praised: so shall I be saved from mine enemies.
The sorrows of death compassed me, and the floods of ungodly men made me afraid.
The sorrows of hell compassed me about: the snares of death prevented me.

In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried unto my God: he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him,
even into his ears.
Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations also of the hills moved and were shaken, because he was wroth.
There went up a smoke out of his nostrils, and fire out of his mouth devoured: coals were kindled by it.

He bowed the heavens also, and came down: and darkness
was
 under his feet.
And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly: yea, he did fly upon the wings of the wind.

He made darkness his secret place; his pavilion round about him
were dark waters
and thick clouds of the skies.

At the brightness
that was before him his thick clouds passed, hail
stones and coals of fire.

The LORD also thundered in the heavens, and the Highest gave his voice; hail
stones and coals of fire.
Yea, he sent out his arrows, and scattered them; and he shot out lightnings, and discomfited them.
Then the channels of waters were seen, and the foundations of the world were discovered at thy rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of the breath of thy nostrils.
He sent from above, he took me, he drew me out of many waters.
He delivered me from my strong enemy, and from them which hated me: for they were too strong for me.
They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay.
He brought me forth also into a large place; he delivered me, because he delighted in me.
The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.
For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God.

For all his judgments
were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.
I was also upright before him, and I kept myself from mine iniquity.
Therefore hath the LORD recompensed me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in his eyesight.
With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful; with an upright man thou wilt shew thyself upright;
With the pure thou wilt shew thyself pure; and with the froward thou wilt shew thyself froward.
For thou wilt save the afflicted people; but wilt bring down high looks.
For thou wilt light my candle: the LORD my God will enlighten my darkness.
For by thee I have run through a troop; and by my God have I leaped over a wall.

As for God, his way
is perfect: the word of the LORD is tried: he
is a buckler to all those that trust in him.

For who
is God save the LORD? or who
is a rock save our God?
It is God that girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect.

He maketh my feet like hinds’
feet, and setteth me upon my high places.
He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.
Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation: and thy right hand hath holden me up, and thy gentleness hath made me great.
Thou hast enlarged my steps under me, that my feet did not slip.
I have pursued mine enemies, and overtaken them: neither did I turn again till they were consumed.
I have wounded them that they were not able to rise: they are fallen under my feet.
For thou hast girded me with strength unto the battle: thou hast subdued under me those that rose up against me.
Thou hast also given me the necks of mine enemies; that I might destroy them that hate me.

They cried, but
there was none to save
them: even
 unto the LORD, but he answered them not.
Then did I beat them small as the dust before the wind: I did cast them out as the dirt in the streets.

Thou hast delivered me from the strivings of the people;
and
 thou hast made me the head of the heathen: a people
whom
 I have not known shall serve me.
As soon as they hear of me, they shall obey me: the strangers shall submit themselves unto me.
The strangers shall fade away, and be afraid out of their close places.

The LORD liveth; and blessed
be my rock; and let the God of my salvation be exalted.
It is God that avengeth me, and subdueth the people under me.
He delivereth me from mine enemies: yea, thou liftest me up above those that rise up against me: thou hast delivered me from the violent man.
Therefore will I give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen, and sing praises unto thy name.
Great deliverance giveth he to his king; and sheweth mercy to his anointed, to David, and to his seed for evermore.
steinsaltz: לַמְנַצֵּחַ, לְעֶבֶד ה', לְדָוִד, אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לַה' אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת בְּיוֹם, בפרק הזמן שבו הִצִּיל ה' אוֹתוֹ מִכַּף כָּל אֹיְבָיו וּמִיַּד שָׁאוּל.
וַיֹּאמַר דוד: אֶרְחָמְךָ, אוהַב אותך, ה' חִזְקִי, מקור חוזקי, מחזקי.

ה' סַלְעִי, כמו על הסלע המוצק אוכל להישען עליך, להתרומם או לחסות בצלך כדי להינצל מפורענויות, וּמְצוּדָתִי, מבצרי וּמְפַלְטִי. ה' מציל אותי גם באופן פעיל. אֵלִי, צוּרִי, סלעי, חוזקי שאֶחֱסֶה בּוֹ, מָגִנִּי וְקֶרֶן יִשְׁעִי, כוח ישועתי, מִשְׂגַּבִּי, המעוז הגבוה שלי. הביטויים שבפסוק משקפים הגנות ואופני תמיכה גדלים והולכים.
מְהֻלָּל אֶקְרָא ה', תמיד אני מהלל את ה' בתפילתי הואיל וּמִן אֹיְבַי אִוָּשֵׁעַ. מכל הסכנות שנקלעתי אליהן בחיי ומכל רדיפותי ניצלתי –
אֲפָפוּנִי, סבבו אותי חֶבְלֵי, חבלים הכורכים ומושכים אל מָוֶת, ובמובן נוסף: חבלי ייסורים, וְנַחֲלֵי בְלִיַּעַל, נחלים של רשעות, או: זרמים בלתי נשלטים יְבַעֲתוּנִי, הפחידו אותי.
חֶבְלֵי שְׁאוֹל, קבר סְבָבוּנִי, קִדְּמוּנִי מוֹקְשֵׁי מָוֶת, מלכודות שהנכנס אליהן עלול שלא לצאת מהן חי.
בַּצַּר לִי אֶקְרָא לה', וְאֶל אֱלֹהַי אֲשַׁוֵּעַ, והוא יִשְׁמַע מֵהֵיכָלוֹ את קוֹלִי, וְשַׁוְעָתִי ששיוועתי לְפָנָיו תָּבוֹא בְאָזְנָיו.

בחלקו השני של המזמור מתוארת התגלות ה' בפאר ובעצמה. התגלות זו אינה קשורה דווקא למאורעותיו של דוד. תיאור כולל זה מזכיר מאורעות התגלות גדולים, כגון מעמד הר סיני: וַתִּגְעַשׁ וַתִּרְעַשׁ הָאָרֶץ, וּמוֹסְדֵי, יסודות ההָרִים יִרְגָּזוּ, ינועו וירעדו, וַיִּתְגָּעֲשׁוּ, כִּי חָרָה לוֹ. ה' זעם על האויבים.
מרוב כעס וחמימות עָלָה עָשָׁן בְּאַפּוֹ, וְאֵשׁ היוצאת מִפִּיו תֹּאכֵל, גֶּחָלִים, ניצוצות בָּעֲרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ. הוא הופיע באופן מבהיל.
וַיֵּט, ה' הִטה את השָׁמַיִם, כופף אותם כלפי מטה וַיֵּרַד, וַעֲרָפֶל היה תַּחַת רַגְלָיו.

ai_explanation_en: This is the introduction to David’s song, spoken after God rescued him from all his enemies and from Saul.
David says that he loves God and recognizes Him as the source of his strength and support.
God is David’s rock, fortress, refuge, shield, and high stronghold; these images describe increasingly broad forms of protection and support.
David calls to God with praise because his deliverance from all dangers and persecutions comes from Him.
David describes death and suffering as surrounding him, while currents of wickedness frighten him.
He feels surrounded by the dangers of Sheol and by deadly traps from which no one emerges alive.
In his distress David calls to God, and God hears his voice and prayer as it reaches Him.
God’s revelation is described with splendor and power: the earth and mountains shake before His anger at the enemies. The description recalls great revelations such as Mount Sinai.
Smoke and fire rise from God’s anger, and burning coals blaze from Him; His appearance is terrifying.
God bends the heavens and descends, with darkness beneath His feet.
God rides a cherub and flies on the wings of the wind; the revelation of the Divine Presence is accompanied by a powerful wind.
God spreads darkness as His hiding place and shelter, surrounded by heavy clouds and dark waters.
From the concealing clouds emerge radiance, hail, and fiery coals; these are forms of revelation breaking through the concealment.
God thunders from the heavens, and His voice is described together with hail and fiery coals as a sign of divine power.
God sends His arrows and scatters the enemies, while many lightning flashes terrify and break them; the whole world is shaken by His revelation.
God’s rebuke and the breath of His anger expose the channels of water and the foundations of the world; the depths are revealed and all reality is shaken.
Alongside the description of God’s greatness in the world, the personal relationship is shown: God sends His hand from above, takes David, and draws him out of deep waters.
God saves David from a strong enemy and from haters who have become stronger than he is.
The enemies confronted David on his day of crisis, but God became his support.
God brought David out of distress into an open place and rescued him from trouble through personal providence and miraculous means.
God rewards David according to his righteousness and clean hands.
David says that he kept God’s ways and did not turn away from Him.
All of God’s judgments were before David’s eyes, and he did not remove His statutes from himself.
David was wholehearted with God and guarded himself from his sin.
God repaid David according to his righteousness and clean hands, which were before Him.
God’s kindness follows His way: He acts kindly with the kindhearted and with a wholehearted person He acts wholeheartedly.
With the pure God acts purely, while with the crooked person He proceeds in a crooked way.
God saves the poor and humble and brings down the proud; He treats people measure for measure.
God lights David’s lamp and dispels his darkness, meaning that He illuminates David’s life.
With God’s help David pursues or crushes an enemy troop, and with his God he leaps over walls.
God’s way is perfect, and His word and promise are free of every flaw; He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
There is no deity or stronghold besides God, and therefore those who take refuge in Him receive the protection they need.
God girds David with strength and success and makes his way straight and complete.
God makes David’s feet steady like those of deer and sets him on his heights and in his strength.
God teaches David’s hands for battle and gives his arms the strength of a firm bronze bow.
God gives David the shield of His salvation, supports him with His right hand, and enlarges him through His humility—His willingness to descend and help.
God enables David to take broad and rapid steps without his ankles slipping.
With this strength David pursues and overtakes his enemies and does not turn back until they are destroyed.
David strikes down his enemies; they cannot rise and fall beneath his feet.
God strengthens David for battle and brings those who rise against him down beneath him.
Because of God, David’s enemies flee before him, and he destroys those who hate him.
The enemies cry for help, but they have no deliverer; they appeal to God, and He does not answer them.
David depicts the destruction of his enemies as dust scattered by the wind and mud poured into the streets.
God saves David from disputes within his people and places him at the head of nations; even peoples he did not know accept his authority.
Nations that hear of David from a distance obey his commands, while foreign enemies lie and flatter him out of fear of his firm position.
Foreign peoples wither and lose their strength, and are forced to leave their fortresses and places of protection in panic.
David concludes by declaring that God lives and works salvation, that God is his rock, and that his saving God will be exalted.
God gives David vengeance and brings peoples under his authority.
God delivers David from his enemies and from those who rise against him, exalts him, and saves him from a violent man.
Therefore David gives thanks to God even among the nations and sings to His name.
God increases the salvations of David the king and shows kindness to His anointed—David and his descendants—forever.

did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? After describing the great storm, the psalm turns to personal deliverance: the Lord reaches out His hand and draws David out of deep waters.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? הביטוי "ויוציאני למרחב" מציב ניגוד בין הצרה והסכנה לבין מרחב פתוח, המסמל הצלה וחירות.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? הביטוי "ויוציאני למרחב" מציב ניגוד בין הצרה והסכנה לבין מרחב פתוח, המסמל הצלה וחירות.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The phrase “He brought me out into a spacious place” contrasts trouble and danger with open space, symbolizing deliverance and freedom.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? דוד מתאר את הכוח שה' מעניק לו באמצעות שתי תמונות ציוריות: ריצה מול גדוד ודילוג על חומה.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? דוד מתאר את הכוח שה' מעניק לו באמצעות שתי תמונות ציוריות: ריצה מול גדוד ודילוג על חומה.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? David describes the strength the Lord gives him through two vivid images: running against a troop and leaping over a wall.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? ה' מתואר כמי שמשווה את רגלי דוד לרגלי אילות ומעמיד אותו על במות—דימויים לזריזות, יציבות ויכולת להתמודד עם גבהים.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? ה' מתואר כמי שמשווה את רגלי דוד לרגלי אילות ומעמיד אותו על במות—דימויים לזריזות, יציבות ויכולת להתמודד עם גבהים.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The Lord is described as making David’s feet like the feet of a deer and setting him on high places—images of agility, stability, and the ability to face great heights.

did_you_know.text: הידעת? המזמור מסתיים בהרחבת ההודיה מדוד עצמו אל שושלתו: ה' עושה חסד למשיחו, לדוד ולזרעו עד עולם.
did_you_know.text_he: הידעת? המזמור מסתיים בהרחבת ההודיה מדוד עצמו אל שושלתו: ה' עושה חסד למשיחו, לדוד ולזרעו עד עולם.
did_you_know.text_en: Did you know? The psalm ends by extending thanksgiving beyond David himself to his dynasty: the Lord shows steadfast love to His anointed, to David and his descendants forever.
